content: KIAA1107 is a protein in humans encoded by the KIAA1107 gene. This protein is serine-rich, and its expression has been observed to increase in the white matter of brain lesions associated with Multiple Sclerosis. The KIAA1107 gene is a protein-coding gene located on chromosome 1 in Homo sapiens. Its genomic location spans from 92,067,052 base pairs to 92,184,723 base pairs from the p-terminal, covering a total of 17,672 bases. The gene contains nine known exons. The uncharacterized protein KIAA1107 is composed of 1,401 amino acids in its most common variant, isoform A, which is found in humans. The molecular weight of this protein is approximately 156 kDa. KIAA1107 has a higher frequency of serine and aspartate residues and a lower frequency of tyrosine residues compared to the average human protein. Specifically, serine constitutes 10% of the protein, making it serine-rich, while tyrosine accounts for only 2.7%, which is below the average for human proteins. Transcription of the KIAA1107 gene produces six different mRNA variants, including four alternatively spliced forms and two unspliced forms. Variant A is the most common and longest form, containing all nine exons in their standard configuration. Variant B includes seven exons (exons 3–9) in their standard form. Variant C-U contains a single exon, which is an alternatively spliced form of exon 8. Variant D includes five exons (exons 1–4 and 5a), with exons 1–4 in their standard form and exon 5 in an alternative form. Variant E contains three exons, which are alternatively spliced forms of exons 3, 4, and 5. Variant F-U contains one exon, which is an alternatively spliced form of exon 5a, also found in variant D. The KIAA1107 protein contains a conserved domain known as DUF4596, located between amino acids 1311 and 1354. The function of this domain remains unknown. The expression of KIAA1107 is not ubiquitous in humans. It is predominantly expressed in the brain, with lower levels of expression observed in the bladder, mammary gland, muscle, prostate, and testis. Within the brain, the highest expression levels are found in the pineal gland, prefrontal cortex, cingulate cortex, and subthalamic nucleus. KIAA1107 has been found to be overexpressed in the white matter of brains with Multiple Sclerosis lesions compared to control white matter. In non-diseased samples, KIAA1107 expression is negligible, whereas in diseased samples, its expression is among the highest of all genes, falling within the 95th to 98th percentile of expression levels. Orthologs of KIAA1107 are present in most vertebrates. The most distant homolog identified is in the Amazon molly, a species of fish. No homologs have been found in sharks or rays, suggesting that KIAA1107 originated in fish. There are no human paralogs for KIAA1107.
